problems: Water Carrier, Village Elder and High Priest have straight, separately boxed lower legs that read as trousers rather than long wraps or robes. The Water Carrier’s square neckline and contrasting chest patch reinforce a tank-top impression.
The Reed Weaver’s bundle emerges directly behind the head like an oversized reed crown. Its carrying attachment is unclear, while the diagonal wrap reads as a rigid slab.
The Village Elder’s symmetrical front panels resemble a vest with a square collar rather than a broad wool shawl. This weakens the Bronze Age garment language despite the appropriate staff.

The trader’s striped mantle forms a long, straight board over one leg. The headwrap and stripes establish some difference, but the variable clothing colours overlap the villagers, and much of the balance scale disappears against the body.
Fine edging, small beads and narrow colour strips contribute little at stream size. The strongest recognition currently comes from props rather than garment construction.

ALL long garments (Water Carrier, Field Tender, Village Elder, High Priest) are built as one tube per leg with a visible crotch split, so every robe and tunic reads as loose trousers or pyjamas/hospital scrubs, not a Bronze Age wrap skirt or robe. Nobody has a flared A-line skirt or kilt silhouette.

Main linen is coloured shirt:light, so it renders as mint green and salmon pink. Person 1 of Water Carrier and of Field Tender comes out pink, nearly the same as their skin, and reads as naked or as pastel scrubs. The bible says cloth is 'dyed sparingly', so undyed linen should be cream and the dye should go on the small parts.

Water Carrier: the 'shoulder cloth' is a flat dark slab (accent:dark) stuck on the right chest at y 0.42. At stream scale it reads as a modern breast pocket or phone pouch. The one-leg stripe (legL 'shirt' box, 0.15 wide) reads as a tracksuit-trouser stripe. The 'wrap skirt' has no wrap: no overlap edge, no flare. The jar on the head is good and should stay.

Field Tender: the sun headcloth is a white cube (flat 0.36x0.08 top plus side plates) that reads as a chef's toque or paper hat, not cloth. Its side flaps sit flush against the cheeks. The hoe blade is a tiny T at the top that reads as a rake or a pickaxe. The knee tunic over split legs looks like a shirt and shorts. Its silhouette is close to the Water Carrier's: both a plain tube body with something on the head.

Reed Weaver: the reed sheaf fans out radially from behind the head (cape cylinders 1.4-1.54 tall, tilted outward). From the front, and even more from above, it reads as a feathered war bonnet or crown, which is the biggest misread in the set. The one-shoulder wrap is two flat slabs rotated -0.55. They stand off the bare chest and read as a messenger-bag strap or a slate board, with the accent stripe floating in front. pants:light shorts come out as grey gym shorts.

Village Elder: the 'broad wool shawl' is two front panels with a collar box and a gap down the middle. It reads as a modern waistcoat, and in the olive role colour as a hi-vis vest. The accent:light strip at hip level (hips y 0.07) reads as a trouser waistband, which makes the rest look like vest plus trousers. There is no headgear at all, so from above the elder is a bare flat-top head. The knob staff makes it read as a weaker copy of the priest.

High Priest: strong symbol of office (the tall staff with a sun disc is the best piece in the set), but the body is cream on cream on a sand-coloured ground and almost vanishes at stream scale. The diagonal ochre mantle slab (hips 0.22x0.65, rot z -0.5) pokes out past the torso edge at the bottom. The chest disc sits off-centre over it, like a gong hung on a strap. The wrapped headdress (cream cylinders plus a dome) reads as a bread roll or shower cap and is very close in shape and colour to the leader's headwrap. The ochre shoulder boxes rise to y 0.61 beside the face and frame it like a cardboard collar.

Far-Bank River Trader: the horizontal stripe boxes on the front mantle are NOT rotated with the 0.42-rad diagonal panel, so they stick out past its edges and float. The headcloth 'tail' (cape box, y -0.31 to +0.34 from the cape origin) sticks UP beside the head like a plank. The mantle end on legL plus tassels turns the left leg into a single striped legwarmer. The tall banded cylinder hat reads as a tin can or fez and repeats the priest's cream dome. The palette (ochre, cream, grey) is the same as the locals', so nothing says 'from far away' at a distance. The lapis collar disc (hips y 0.6) partly covers the chin.

Distinctness from above: Water Carrier, Field Tender and Elder are all a plain rectangle body with a flat top head. Headgear is the only differentiator, and two of them have none (Water Carrier's jar aside). Elder and Priest both carry a knobbed staff.
fix:
Water Carrier: Keep the head jar, but make its support pad visible and add a dark recessed mouth. Replace the square shirt neckline and chest patch with a continuous one-shoulder linen drape. Give the lower wrap an offset overlap and uneven hem rather than two rectangular trouser legs. Field Tender: Preserve the hoe and shorter tunic silhouette. Extend the sun cloth visibly down the back and sides, and add an overlapping tunic hem so the lower garment does not read as shorts; keep the shaft seated in the hand. Reed Weaver: Shift the sheaf behind one shoulder, with asymmetric tips clear of the head silhouette. Add a visible shoulder harness connected to the bundle’s lashings. Fit the diagonal cloth against the torso and narrow its projecting edges. Village Elder: Replace the vest-like front with a broad, asymmetric shawl crossing the chest and continuing over the shoulders; use a chunky contrasting woven border. Add an offset ankle-wrap closure. High Priest: Retain the tall sun staff, large pectoral and cream/turquoise palette. Rework the lower robe into overlapping, staggered panels and broaden the shoulder colour area for overhead recognition. River Trader: Establish a fixed deep-blue, ochre and cream textile palette distinct from the villagers. Shorten and step the mantle’s hanging edge, fit it closely to the torso and thigh, and place the balance farther outside the body silhouette so both pans read. Across all kits: eliminate exposed default-shirt edging. Keep upper wraps hip-bound and moving lower panels attached to their respective legs; do not solve the robe silhouette with one rigid piece spanning both limbs. Check shoulder, hem and prop clearance in walking poses at the actual stream camera. / GLOBAL: (a) Make every robe, tunic or skirt below the waist a hips-bone skirt that hides the leg split. Use a front panel and a back panel at hips [0,-0.15,±0.165] size [0.54,0.34,0.03], plus side panels [±0.27,-0.15,0] size [0.03,0.34,0.32], so it is wider than the legs (an A-line flare). For ankle length, continue on each leg only from the knee down (leg tubes from y -0.4 to -0.72), with the leg tube's inner faces removed so no crotch seam shows. (b) Main linen as fixed undyed #ead7aa or #d2bb87. Put the wearer's role colours ONLY on dyed wool: shawls, mantles, belts, headbands, hem borders (accent, hat, shirt:dark). That keeps each person unique and stops the pastel scrubs and skin-tone clash.

WATER CARRIER: keep the head jar and head pad. Replace the chest slab with a real shoulder cloth: a hat-role wool box draped over the LEFT shoulder only, on hips [0.17,0.5,0] size [0.26,0.14,0.36], plus a front fall [0.17,0.32,0.165] size [0.2,0.3,0.03] and a back fall, ending in a 2-3 cube fringe. Delete the legL stripe. Make the wrap skirt an ankle-length cream skirt per GLOBAL (a), with a diagonal overlap edge: a thin accent box on hips at [0.08,-0.15,0.185], size [0.04,0.36,0.015], rot z 0.15. Add a bare-arm look (keep 'sleeves' hidden) and a hair-colour tied knot visible on top (a sphere at head [0,0.36,-0.08]) under the jar.

FIELD TENDER: rebuild the sun headcloth as soft cloth: a head cap box [0.34,0.06,0.32] at y 0.33, plus a long back drape on the head bone [0,0.05,-0.17] size [0.36,0.4,0.03] that falls to the shoulders, a hat:dark tie band around the forehead, and NO side plates on the cheeks. Make the hoe read as a hoe: a bronze blade box #b68942 size [0.22,0.16,0.04] set at a right angle to the shaft, and keep the shaft on armR only, ending at the hand. Knee-length belted cream tunic as a hips skirt per GLOBAL (a), with a shirt:dark belt and a hanging belt end. Bare shins, sandals.

REED WEAVER: move the sheaf so it reads as carried, not worn. Make a tight bundle of 5-6 reeds held under the left arm, on armL, lying near-horizontal (rot x about -1.3), 1.2 long, tied with two #6d4c32 bands. Or put them on the back diagonally (cape bone, rot z 0.6) with the tips clearing ONE shoulder, never fanning above the head. Remove all outward splay. Make the one-shoulder wrap sit on the skin: z just 0.145-0.15, thickness 0.02. Better, use three short stepped boxes following the diagonal rather than one slab standing off the chest, and put the accent stripe at the SAME rotation and z+0.01. Replace the grey shorts with a short wrapped kilt (hips skirt per GLOBAL (a) to y -0.3) in cream with an accent hem, and add a hat-role headband so the head is not bare.

VILLAGE ELDER: replace the vest panels with a real broad shawl. It should be one wide hat-role wool mass over BOTH shoulders: a hips box [0,0.52,0] size [0.62,0.12,0.40], plus arm-bone shoulder caps on armL and armR [0,-0.05,0] size [0.19,0.16,0.21] in the same colour, plus a back fall on cape. Add a fringe of 5-6 small cubes along the front lower edge at y 0.3. No centre gap, no collar box. Delete the hip strip at y 0.07. Use an ankle-length cream robe per GLOBAL (a) with a broad accent hem border. Add headgear: a wrapped wool cap or a hair-coloured long beard box on the chin [0,-0.02,0.15] size [0.2,0.14,0.04], plus a fillet band. Make the staff a plain crooked or forked walking stick (a #6d4c32 shaft with an angled top piece), with NO round knob, so it never echoes the priest's staff.

HIGH PRIEST: keep the sun-disc staff exactly. Fix the contrast: make the mantle a big turquoise #429d9b and ochre #b68942 woven mantle over both shoulders. Use hips [0,0.5,0] size [0.6,0.14,0.42] with arm caps, a cape in #429d9b with an ochre border, and a front fall that sits flat on the chest (z 0.16, no diagonal slab sticking out). Centre the chest disc at hips [0,0.32,0.19], hung from two cords that meet it. Lower the ochre shoulder boxes to y 0.56 so they don't frame the face. Make the headdress taller and unmistakable: a tall tapering wrapped headdress (stacked cylinders narrowing upward to about y 0.75) in cream with three turquoise bands and a small bronze sun disc at the front, so its shape differs clearly from the leader's.

FAR-BANK RIVER TRADER: rotate every stripe box with its panel (same rot z 0.42, z +0.012), or use separate stripe slabs that lie within the panel bounds. Move the headcloth tail to hang DOWN from the back of the head: head bone [0,0.05,-0.17] size [0.14,0.45,0.03], ending at the shoulder blades. Move the leg-mounted mantle end and the tassels to the hips bone as a knee-length striped wrap skirt, with the fringe along its hem. Give him a foreign palette absent from the townspeople: bold #d9534f red and #365f86 lapis stripes on the mantle and headwrap, no ochre or cream as the dominant colour. Make the headwrap a low, wide, lumpy turban (two offset cylinders, height ≤0.18, wider than the head) instead of a tall can. Make the lapis collar a flat wide ring at hips y 0.56, below the chin. Add a traveller's bundle on the back: a cape-bone roll of folded textiles [0,-0.15,-0.08] size [0.46,0.22,0.22] tied with #6d4c32 cords, so 'from far away' reads from above. Keep the balance scale in the hand.
